evidence.quote: Northwind Robotics today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Helios Sensors in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $2.1 billion.
The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2024, subject to regulatory approvals and approval by Helios shareholders.
Northwind Robotics has agreed to buy Helios Sensors for about $2.1 billion in cash, the company said on Monday.
In March, the European Commission opened an in-depth investigation into the deal, citing concerns about the supply of lidar components.
The review is ongoing, and a decision is not expected before June.
Northwind has completed its purchase of Helios Sensors after clearing its final regulatory hurdle in the United States.
The European Commission has opened an in-depth investigation to assess the proposed acquisition of Helios Sensors by Northwind Robotics.
The waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act expired on April 2, clearing the deal in the United States. The European Commission's review remains pending.
Northwind Robotics is in advanced talks to acquire Helios Sensors, according to people familiar with the matter.
Helios shareholders voted overwhelmingly on Tuesday to approve the takeover by Northwind Robotics.

The European Commission has approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the proposed acquisition of Helios Sensors by Northwind Robotics. The approval is conditional on full compliance with commitments offered by Northwind.
Under the remedies, Northwind must license Helios' lidar patents to rival manufacturers on fair terms for ten years.
With all required regulatory approvals now obtained, Northwind expects the transaction to close in the third quarter of 2024.

report.title: Northwind Robotics' acquisition of Helios Sensors: status as of June 30, 2024

sentences.text: As of June 30, 2024, Northwind Robotics had not yet completed its acquisition of Helios Sensors.
All required approvals had been obtained — US clearance on April 2 and conditional EU approval on June 12 — and Northwind expected the deal to close in the third quarter of 2024.
An April report that the deal had already closed is contradicted by the original sources.
Talks were first reported in November 2023, based on anonymous sources.
On January 15, 2024, Northwind announced a definitive agreement to acquire Helios for about $2.1 billion in cash.
The company expected the transaction to close in the second half of 2024, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
Helios shareholders approved the takeover on February 20.
On March 18, the European Commission opened an in-depth investigation, citing concerns about the supply of lidar components.
In the United States, the HSR waiting period expired on April 2.
On June 12, the Commission approved the deal subject to commitments, including ten-year licensing of Helios lidar patents to rivals.
The April 5 report of completion appears to have conflated US clearance with closing: the US event it describes matches the HSR expiry, while the EU review was still pending in May.
The four January articles republish the same press release, so they count as one independent source.
The November 2023 talks report rests on a single anonymous-sourced account and could not be independently confirmed.
Whether closing occurred on schedule falls after the cutoff and is outside the scope of this report.
